VPE table allocation and pending and property table sizing and layout.

findings.text: VPE doorbell affinity handling distinguishes destroyed versus live virtual processors. When no mapping known as VMAPP remains it either rejects under eager policy or records the first requested processor and finishes without hardware action under lazy policy. For live entries it favors a processor sharing the current table mask, retains the current processor when it remains acceptable, otherwise takes the first requested processor, and only when the target differs updates the cached processor index, requests a move known as VMOVP, applies a vendor specific full invalidate when present, relocates the proxy doorbell, then publishes effective affinity.

Affinity mutation uses two layers. The virtual machine mapping lock is held when the ITS list map is in use to serialize against concurrent mapping state changes. A per VPE processor selector lock guards the cached processor index because virtual LPI paths may sample it concurrently and the descriptor lock alone is insufficient, so any path evaluating that index must hold the same guard.

Lookup for a version 4.1 ITS prefers a per CPU cached instance when present. Otherwise it scans the global ITS list for the first instance advertising 4.1 support and returns it. When neither yields a candidate it returns null to signal absence.

Version 4 virtual CPU affinity multiplexes four requests known as SCHEDULE_VPE and DESCHEDULE_VPE and COMMIT_VPE and INVALL_VPE. Schedule programs redistributor tables for residency, deschedule revokes residency while saving status hints, commit waits for pending table parsing to finish, and invalidate refreshes caches across the fabric. Any other request code is rejected.

Version 4 scheduling derives property and pending base addresses from the virtual machine property page and the per VPE pending page, programs GICR_VPROPBASER and GICR_VPENDBASER with shareability attributes when supported, and marks the pending entry valid with pending last hint and direct injection allowance preserved. Descheduling clears validity and captures the returned direct injection and pending last indications into soft state.
Commit is a no-op on platforms lacking a dirty indication for pending validity. Otherwise it polls the pending base control until the dirty indication clears, warning if the bounded wait expires.

Version 4 full invalidation holds the virtual machine mapping lock throughout the scan. It walks ITS instances, ignores those without version 4 support, and when the list map is active ignores instances with no virtual LPIs for that virtual machine. It issues a single invalidate to the first eligible ITS because reaching redistributors once suffices, then stops.

Version 4 mask and unmask adjust the enabled property through the parent LPI record rather than calling into the parent chip, then request invalidation of that LPI. Invalidation uses a direct redistributor operation when the platform supports direct LPIs, otherwise it maps the VPE into a shared proxy device under the proxy lock and issues the command through that proxy event.

Doorbell pending control only supports the pending state and rejects other states. With direct LPI support it sets or clears the doorbell LPI at the redistributor owning the current processor index and synchronizes after clear. Without that support it routes set and clear commands through the proxy device. Retrigger is defined as setting pending and reports success as a boolean inversion.

The version 4 VPE chip advertises a name identifying GICv4 VPE handling and wires mask, unmask, parent end of interrupt, affinity, retrigger, pending state control, and virtual CPU affinity operations.

Version 4.1 doorbell invalidation is broadcast oriented. It locates a 4.1 ITS and asks hardware with INVDB to invalidate the doorbell across redistributors, doing nothing further when no such ITS exists.
Version 4.1 mask and unmask update the parent LPI enabled property in the same manner as version 4 but follow with the broadcast doorbell invalidate instead of the version 4 invalidate path.

Version 4.1 virtual CPU affinity multiplexes the same four request codes with version specific handlers. Schedule enables residency with group enables and VPE identity, deschedule handles blocking versus non-blocking exits distinctly, commit reuses the pending parse wait, and invalidate targets the current redistributor. Other codes are rejected.

Version 4.1 blocking deschedule serializes the pending last update against concurrent doorbell interrupts with the per VPE lock while clearing validity with pending last clear and doorbell armed, so a clear readback guarantees a future doorbell on new work. Non-blocking deschedule clears validity with pending last set and records that the processor will return. Version 4.1 invalidate reads the current processor under the selector lock and invalidates at that redistributor.

The version 4.1 VPE chip advertises a distinct name and wires mask, unmask, parent end of interrupt, shared affinity handling, and version specific virtual CPU affinity, without retrigger or generic pending state operations.

Virtual SGI configuration is built from per VPE stored priority, enable, and group for the addressed SGI number plus a clear flag distinguishing reconfiguration from pending clear. The resulting command is sent to the first 4.1 ITS on the assumption that eager mapping at activation makes that destination valid.
Virtual SGI mask and unmask flip the stored enable flag for that SGI and reissue configuration without clearing pending, leaving any pending indication unchanged.
Virtual SGI affinity has no host meaning because delivery targets a VPE. The handler records the requested mask as effective and reports success without hardware action.

Virtual SGI pending control only supports pending state. Setting pending encodes VPE identity and virtual interrupt number into the SGI generation control of a 4.1 ITS. Clearing pending reissues SGI configuration with the clear indication set.

Reading virtual SGI pending status nests the per VPE processor selector lock outside the target redistributor lock to stabilize both the destination processor and the two register access sequence. It selects the VPE with GICR_VSGIR then polls GICR_VSGIPENDR until the busy indication clears.

The SGI status poll is bounded to about one second with microsecond spacing and processor relaxation. On expiry it emits a rate limited diagnostic and fails the read, so callers must handle a not retrievable outcome. Success extracts the bit for the addressed SGI number.

Virtual SGI property update only honors the SGI property request known as PROP_UPDATE_VSGI and rejects others. It stores the supplied priority and group into the per VPE SGI record then reconfigures without clearing pending.
The virtual SGI chip advertises a version 4.1 SGI name and wires mask, unmask, affinity, pending set, pending get, and virtual CPU affinity operations.

The SGI domain provisions sixteen entries per VPE with zero priority, disabled, and group clear, binds each virtual interrupt to its SGI number with the SGI chip and VPE cookie, and marks them non lazy. Freeing is a no-op. Activation writes the initial configuration. Deactivation disables then issues separate reconfigure and pending clear commands because one command cannot do both.

VPE identity comes from a bounded allocator with a defined maximum and is returned on free. Initialization allocates identity, then a pending table page, then a VPE table entry, unwinding prior steps on failure, initializes the per VPE lock, records identity and table, zeroes the mapping reference count, and marks the proxy event invalid when the platform lacks residual VPE identity support. Teardown is a no-op when initialization never completed, otherwise it unmaps the proxy doorbell and releases identity and pending storage.

VPE domain allocation reserves a power of two LPI bitmap and property storage, initializes the mapping lock, and picks the 4.1 chip when residual identity exists. Each VPE records its doorbell LPI, completes identity and table setup, allocates its parent interrupt, binds the chip, sets its bitmap position, and enables resend while in progress, unwinding on failure. Freeing releases parents, checks virtual machine ownership, clears bitmap positions, tears down VPEs, resets records, and frees LPI and property storage once empty.

Activation pins each VPE to the first online processor and publishes that affinity, doing no mapping work unless eager policy requires it, otherwise mapping then invalidating on every version 4 ITS. Deactivation does nothing unless eager, otherwise unmaps on every version 4 ITS and flushes the pending table to the point of coherence when a 4.1 ITS is present and no mappings remain.

Table base updates require the ITS to be both disabled and quiescent, otherwise results are unpredictable per GITS_CTLR handling. The helper treats already quiescent and disabled as success and otherwise proceeds to force quiescence, with the remainder of that sequence outside these fragments.
Each virtual processor provides sixteen virtual SGIs numbered zero through fifteen.

Pending parse completion polls with single unit sleeps up to five hundred iterations when dirty tracking exists. SGI status polling allows one million microsecond spaced attempts, about one second, before reporting failure.

Unsupported pending states, unsupported virtual CPU commands, and affinity on a destroyed VPE under eager mapping report EINVAL. Allocation shortfalls report ENOMEM. Expired SGI status reads report ENXIO. Successful affinity updates report IRQ_SET_MASK_OK_DONE for VPEs and IRQ_SET_MASK_OK for virtual SGIs.

Observed virtual processor state includes a mapping reference count, cached processor index, owning virtual machine link, numeric VPE identity, pending table page, doorbell LPI, proxy event, status hints for direct injection and pending last, and per SGI configuration records holding priority, enable, and group. Observed virtual machine state includes property page, doorbell bitmap with base and count, per ITS virtual LPI counts, and a mapping lock.
